title: Workspace activity rollups and curated analytics layer for Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a curated analytics layer that produces workspace-level rollups and route-level cost attributions for the Console product. This ticket covers schema design, dbt models, partitioning/clustering policies, backfill plan, and compatibility views for downstream dashboards. The aim is to replace fragile ad-hoc queries in Looker/Metabase with performant, cost-conscious tables that meet a 15-minute freshness SLA for nearline metrics and nightly full refreshes for historical aggregates.

Background: Current Console dashboards query a mix of raw event streams and denormalized export tables which causes high query cost and inconsistent results. We need a single source-of-truth set of curated tables in the redwood_analytics.console dataset that provide: daily/hourly workspace activity, route token usage, unique active users, session counts, and basic cost attribution by model and route. These tables will be the foundation for Console Console Usage dashboard, billing reconciliations, and routing optimization signals.

Scope:
- Design fact and dimension schemas: workspace_dim, user_dim, route_dim, model_dim, event_fact_raw, workspace_activity_hourly, workspace_activity_daily, route_cost_facts.
- Implement dbt models (incremental where possible) with BigQuery materializations.
- Partition hourly/daily rollups by date; cluster by workspace_id, route_id, model_id.
- Implement deduplication and late-arrival handling for streaming events (using event_ingest_timestamp and event_id).
- Backfill last 18 months with controlled job to avoid quota spikes.
- Expose compat views with old naming to avoid breaking dashboards.
- Add monitoring: freshness checks, row-count delta alerts, and cost estimate per-table in Console.

Non-goals: Detailed chargeback automation and per-token costing inflation adjustments (these will be separate tickets).
acceptance_criteria: A dbt project under models/console/ with modular models for dims and facts exists in the repo and builds successfully via CI
workspace_activity_hourly and workspace_activity_daily tables materialize in redwood_analytics.console and are partitioned by event_date
Hourly rollups meet the 15-minute freshness SLA in 95% of runs (measured by freshness sensors in dbt Cloud / Airflow), with documented SLO and incident playbook
Route-level cost attribution is computed and validated against a sample of billing records (variance < 2%)
Backfill for last 18 months completed without exceeding BigQuery slot quotas or creating duplicate rows
Compatibility views exist for the two most-used legacy queries and dashboards point to the new views
Runbook and confluence doc describing schema, retention, and migration steps are published and linked from the Console docs
